questions.sec: Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide
questions.q: The Friedman curve was the ______ partogram and has a ______ shape.
questions.exp: Friedman curve = 1st partogram, sigmoid curve. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide
questions.q: The alert–action line concept was introduced by ______ on the principle of minimum active-phase dilatation of ______.
questions.exp: Alert/action line introduced by Philpott & Castle; principle: minimum 1 cm/hr in the active phase. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide
questions.q: The modified WHO partogram is based on ______ and plots only the ______, beginning at ______ cervical dilatation.
opts: Previous WHO recommendations; active phase; 4 cm
Recent WHO guidelines; latent phase; 3 cm
questions.exp: Modified WHO partogram: based on previous WHO recommendations; active phase only; plotting begins at 4 cm. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide
questions.q: Which features describe the next-generation partogram (Labour Care Guide)? Select the correct set.
opts: Based on recent WHO guidelines; no alert and action line; first (active) and second stage represented; active phase begins at 5 cm; 7 sections
Based on old WHO; retains alert/action line; only first stage; begins at 4 cm; 3 sections
Based on Friedman; alert line only; latent + active; begins at 3 cm; 5 sections
Based on ACOG; action line only; second stage only; begins at 6 cm; 7 sections
questions.exp: Labour Care Guide: recent WHO, no alert/action lines, represents active first + second stage, active phase from 5 cm, 7 sections. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide
questions.q: The time difference between the alert line and the action line on the modified WHO partogram is:
questions.exp: The action line is drawn 4 hours to the right of the alert line. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Types of partogram
questions.q: Fill up: The Friedman curve plots cervical dilatation against time, while the modified WHO partograph adds the ______ line and the ______ line to it.
questions.exp: The alert line shows the expected rate of progress and the action line, four hours to its right, is the point at which intervention is required. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters
questions.q: On the modified WHO partograph, fetal heart rate is recorded every ______ (every ______ in high risk) and the normal range is ______.
questions.exp: FHR normal 110–160 bpm, recorded every 30 min (every 15 min for high risk). (Book p506)

questions.sec: Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters
questions.q: Match the amniotic fluid code – I : C : M : B.
opts: Intact membrane : colourless fluid : meconium stained : blood stained
questions.exp: I = intact membrane; C = colourless; M = meconium stained; B = blood stained. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters
questions.q: Moulding on the partograph is denoted as:
opts: 0/× = no moulding; +1, +2, +3 = degrees of overlapping of cranial bones
questions.exp: Moulding = overlapping of cranial bones; 0/× no moulding; +1, +2, +3 moulding. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters
questions.q: All of the following are recorded in the upper part of the modified WHO partograph EXCEPT:
opts: Colour and character of the amniotic fluid
Degree of moulding of the fetal skull
questions.exp: The upper part follows the fetus — heart rate, membranes, liquor and moulding; maternal observations belong to the lower part. (Book p506)

questions.sec: Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters
questions.q: In the modified WHO partograph, the interval for fetal parameters is represented by one small box equal to ______, and the three parts of the sheet are ______.
opts: 30 min; upper = fetal parameters, middle = cervicograph, lower = maternal condition
1 hr; upper = maternal, middle = fetal, lower = drugs
15 min; upper = cervicograph, middle = contractions, lower = fetal
2 hr; upper = drugs, middle = fetal, lower = maternal
questions.exp: One small box = 30 min for fetal parameters; upper part fetal, middle part cervicograph, lower part maternal condition. (Book p507)

questions.sec: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
questions.q: The middle part of the modified WHO partograph, plotting cervical dilatation (×) and descent (O) against time (1 box = 1 hr), is called the:
questions.exp: Middle part = cervicograph (cervix plotted as X, descent as O; 1 box = 1 hour). (Book p507)

questions.sec: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
questions.q: Match the cervicograph zone to its meaning — green : yellow (alert) : pink (action).
opts: Normal progress : alert, so shift her to a tertiary centre : intervene once the action line is touched
Alert, so shift her : normal progress : intervene on touching the action line
Intervene at once : alert, so shift her : entirely normal progress
Normal progress : intervene at once : refer her to a tertiary centre
questions.exp: Green means progress is normal, the alert zone means prepare for transfer, and touching the action line means intervention is required. (Book p507)

questions.sec: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
questions.q: The colour-coded zones form the basis of the ______ WHO partogram.
questions.exp: The zones are the basis for the simplified WHO partogram. (Book p507)

questions.sec: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
questions.q: The first plotting of cervical dilatation is always made:
opts: On the alert line (never to the left of it)
To the left of the alert line
questions.exp: First plot is always on the alert line > left of alert line. (Book p507)

questions.sec: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
questions.q: Worked example from the notes: a G2P woman at 4 cm at 4 pm is plotted on the alert line; at 6 pm she is 6 cm and at 8 pm 8 cm. Her progress is:
opts: Normal progress (1 cm/hr, staying left of/on the alert line)
Alert zone – refer to tertiary centre
questions.exp: 4 → 6 → 8 cm over 4 hours = 1 cm/hr, plotted on/left of the alert line = normal progress. (Book p507)

questions.sec: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
questions.q: Fill up: The alert line on the cervicograph is drawn at a dilatation rate of ______ cm per hour from the point of admission, and the action line lies ______ hours to its right.
questions.exp: Crossing the action line means slow progress has persisted for four hours and transfers, augmentation or operative delivery must be considered. (Book p507)

questions.sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
questions.q: Which patient parameters are NOT recorded on the modified WHO partograph?
opts: Respiratory rate, SpO2 and oral fluids consumed
questions.exp: Not recorded: respiratory rate, SpO2, oral fluids consumed. (Book p508)

questions.sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
questions.q: Adequate uterine contractions are defined as:
opts: At least three in 10 minutes, each lasting 45 seconds and raising pressure by 65-75 mmHg
At least five in 10 minutes, each lasting 60 seconds at 100 mmHg
At least two in 10 minutes, each lasting 20 seconds at 30 mmHg
At least three in 15 minutes, each lasting 30 seconds at 50 mmHg
questions.exp: Adequate contractions are three or more in ten minutes, each lasting about 45 seconds with an amplitude of 65-75 mmHg. (Book p508)

questions.sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
questions.q: Contractions are measured by observation over the uterine fundus for ______ every ______.
questions.exp: Observed over fundus for 10 minutes every 30 minutes. (Book p508)

questions.sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
questions.q: More than 5 contractions in 10 min is termed:
questions.exp: >5 contractions in 10 min = tachysystole. (Book p508)

questions.sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
questions.q: Match the shading of contraction duration boxes – dotted : hatched/oblique lines : solid fill.
questions.exp: Dotted <20 sec; hatched 20–40 sec; solid >40 sec (each box = 1 contraction). (Book p508)

questions.sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
questions.q: A contraction lasting ≥60 sec indicates ______; management is ______.
opts: A hypertonic contraction from oxytocin; stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, consider terbutaline
An entirely adequate contraction, so the infusion should be continued unchanged
Tachysystole, for which the rate of oxytocin should be increased
A Bandl's ring forming, which requires immediate caesarean section
questions.exp: A contraction lasting 60 seconds or more is hypertonic and usually drug-induced: stop the infusion, turn her and give a tocolytic if needed. (Book p508)

questions.sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
questions.q: Match the lower-part observation with how it is recorded — 1) Uterine contractions 2) Maternal pulse 3) Urine … A) Five squares per hour shaded according to the duration and strength of each contraction B) Recorded hourly and entered as a dot on the chart C) Recorded at each voiding, with the volume and any protein or acetone noted
questions.exp: Contractions fill five squares an hour, the pulse is plotted hourly, and urine is checked at each void for volume, protein and ketones. (Book p508)

questions.sec: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
questions.q: Arrange the seven sections of the Labour Care Guide in order (Sections 1–7):
opts: Patient & labour details → supportive care → care of baby → care of woman → labour progress → medication → plan of action
Care of woman → care of baby → supportive care → labour progress → medication → plan → details
Labour progress → medication → plan → details → supportive care → baby → woman
Details → baby → woman → supportive care → medication → progress → plan
questions.exp: 1 details, 2 supportive care, 3 baby, 4 woman, 5 labour progress, 6 medication, 7 plan of action. (Book p508)

questions.sec: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
questions.q: The mnemonic for the LCG sections given in the notes is:
opts: Please Save Big Women Lovingly Made
questions.exp: Mnemonic: Smart Beautiful WOMEN Love Me. (Book p509)

questions.sec: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
questions.q: Which statements describe the Labour Care Guide layout and applicability?
opts: Alert box in front of each parameter; used in all women in labour; used at all levels of health care
Alert line drawn diagonally; used only in high-risk women; tertiary centres only
No alert boxes; primigravida only; primary centres
Action line retained; multigravida only; secondary centres
questions.exp: LCG has an alert box before each parameter, is used for all women in labour and at all levels of care. (Book p509)

questions.sec: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
questions.q: Section 2 (Supportive care) of the LCG includes:
opts: Companion, posture, oral fluid (solid food not advisable), pain relief
questions.exp: Supportive care: companion, posture, oral fluid (solids not advisable) and pain relief. (Book p509)

questions.sec: Labour Care Guide: supportive care & alert column
questions.q: Using the WHO Labour Care Guide, a woman at 6 cm moves into the alert column because dilatation has slowed. Contractions are adequate and the fetal heart is normal. What does the guide advise?
opts: Document the deviation, look for and treat the cause, and continue supportive care with closer monitoring
Immediate caesarean section for every entry into the alert column
Reassurance only, because the alert column carries no clinical meaning
Stop monitoring and transfer her out of the labour ward
questions.exp: The alert column is a prompt to reassess and respond to the underlying cause rather than a trigger for automatic surgery. (Book p509)

questions.sec: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
questions.q: Coding for companion, oral fluid and pain relief in the LCG – Y : N : D; which one is an alert feature?
opts: Yes : No : Denied; 'N' is the alert
Yes : None : Done; 'D' is the alert
Young : Normal : Delayed; 'Y' is the alert
questions.exp: Y = yes, N = no (alert), D = denied. (Book p510)

questions.sec: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
questions.q: Posture coding in the LCG – MO : SP : L/L; the alert feature is:
opts: Mobile : supine : left lateral; supine is the alert
Motionless : sitting : lying; sitting is alert
Mobile : semi-prone : lateral; lateral is alert
questions.exp: MO mobile, SP supine (alert), L/L left lateral. (Book p510)

questions.sec: LCG Section 3: care of baby
questions.q: In LCG Section 3, baseline FHR normal is ______, abnormal (alert) is ______, documented every ______.
questions.exp: Normal 110–160; alert <110 or >160; documented every 30 min as per WHO guideline. (Book p510)

questions.sec: LCG Section 3: care of baby
questions.q: FHR deceleration codes – N : E : L : V; which is the alert feature?
opts: No : early : late : variable; late is the alert
None : early : light : very; variable is the alert
Normal : early : late : variable; early is the alert
No : elevated : low : varied; low is the alert
questions.exp: N no, E early, L late (alert), V variable. (Book p510)

questions.sec: LCG Section 3: care of baby
questions.q: Amniotic fluid codes in the LCG and alert features:
opts: I intact, C clear; M meconium-stained and B blood-stained are alerts
I intact, C clear; both alerts
I inadequate, C clear; M is normal
C clear only; I is alert
questions.exp: I intact membrane, C clear fluid; M meconium and B blood-stained are alert features. (Book p510)

questions.sec: LCG Section 3: care of baby
questions.q: Fetal position codes – A : P : T; alerts are:
opts: Occipitoanterior : occipitoposterior : occipitotransverse; P and T are alerts
Anterior : posterior : transverse; only P is alert
Anterior : posterior : transverse; A is alert
Asynclitic : posterior : transverse; T is alert
questions.exp: A = OA; P = OP (alert); T = OT (alert). (Book p510)

questions.sec: LCG Section 3: care of baby
questions.q: Caput and moulding are coded as +/++/+++; the alert feature is:
questions.exp: Caput/moulding +++ is the alert feature. (Book p510)

questions.sec: LCG Section 3: care of the baby
questions.q: Which of the following statements about the WHO Labour Care Guide is TRUE?
opts: It records fetal heart rate, liquor, caput and moulding in the section on the baby, and its alert column prompts a clinical response
It replaces the partograph and no longer records the fetal heart rate
It is intended only for women with obstructed labour or ruptured uterus
It recommends routine amniotomy for every woman as soon as she reaches 4 cm
questions.exp: The Labour Care Guide keeps continuous fetal and maternal observation but replaces rigid time limits with alert thresholds and individualised care. (Book p510)

questions.sec: LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
questions.q: Section 4 (care of woman) records pulse, temperature, BP and urine (protein, acetone). Match the alert thresholds – pulse : systolic BP : diastolic BP : temperature.
questions.exp: Alerts: pulse <60/≥120; SBP <80/≥140; DBP ≥90; temp <35.0/≥37.5 °C; urine P++/A++. (Book p511)

questions.sec: LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
questions.q: Section 5 (progress of labour) – contraction alerts: number in 10 min ______ and duration ______.
questions.exp: Alert: ≤2 or >5 contractions per 10 min; duration <20 or >60 seconds (checked every 30 min). (Book p511)

questions.sec: LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
questions.q: Time-bound alert figures for cervical dilatation in the LCG – at 5 cm : 6 cm : 7 cm : 8 cm : 9 cm.
questions.exp: Time-bound alerts: 5 cm → 6 h, 6 → 5, 7 → 3, 8 → 2.5, 9 → 2 h (mnemonic 6-5-3-2.5-2); at 10 cm second stage, P = time of pushing. (Book p511)

questions.sec: LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
questions.q: WHO maximum duration of second stage – primi without epidural : multi without epidural : with epidural.
questions.exp: Primi 3 h, multi 2 h; add 1 h with epidural. (Book p511)

questions.sec: LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
questions.q: Section 6 (medication) of the LCG records ______ and Section 7 is ______.
opts: Oxytocin, IV fluids, drugs; shared decision-making (assessment and plan)
questions.exp: Section 6: oxytocin, IV fluids, drugs. Section 7: shared decision making – assessment and plan. (Book p511)

questions.sec: LCG Sections 4-7
questions.q: All of the following are recorded in the WHO Labour Care Guide EXCEPT:
opts: A postnatal follow-up plan for six weeks after delivery
Maternal position, mobility, hydration and pain relief
Progress of labour with dilatation, descent and contractions
Medications given and the plan for the next review
questions.exp: The guide covers the woman, the baby, progress, medication and the plan for labour itself; postpartum follow-up is a separate schedule. (Book p511)

units.title: Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide
units.guide: Trace the evolution from Friedman's sigmoid curve through Philpott's alert line to the 2020 Labour Care Guide and what each one plots. Focus for this checkpoint: Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide.

units.title: Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters
units.guide: Record FHR, amniotic fluid codes and moulding grades exactly as they appear in the fetal section of the modified WHO partograph. Focus for this checkpoint: Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters.

units.title: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
units.guide: Interpret the green–yellow–pink zones of the cervicograph and apply the rule that the first plot always goes on the alert line. Focus for this checkpoint: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones.

units.title: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
units.guide: Know what the lower part records, what it omits, and how adequate contractions are counted, timed, shaded and rescued when hypertonic. Focus for this checkpoint: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions.

units.title: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
units.guide: Memorise the seven LCG sections with the mnemonic, the alert-box concept, and how companion, pain relief, fluids and posture are coded. Focus for this checkpoint: Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column.

units.title: LCG Section 3: care of baby
units.guide: Code every fetal parameter of Section 3 and identify which values trigger the red alert box. Focus for this checkpoint: LCG Section 3: care of baby.

units.title: LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
units.guide: Fix the maternal alert thresholds, the contraction and time-bound dilatation alerts, the WHO second-stage limits and the final sections. Focus for this checkpoint: LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan.
